name: Issue UCAN Token
description: Creates a UCAN capability token granting the audience (aud) the specified capabilities (att). By default the venue signs it, valid at this venue only, over resources of identities it hosts that you may grant: your own, those of an identity you sign in as, your agents', or any covered by a grant/<can> right you present. You confer only what you hold. With key, a key in a keyring signs it instead, valid anywhere. Set exp to a future Unix timestamp for a finite lifetime; omitted exp or explicit exp:null mints a genuinely non-expiring token with an explicit null claim. With prf, the venue itself passes on part of grants made to it: the token carries them as proof, every att entry must be covered by one of them, and exp cannot outlive it.

aud.description: Audience DID — who receives this capability (e.g. did:key:z6MkBob...)

att.description: Attenuations — array of {with, can} capability pairs

with.description: Resource: a bare path in the namespace you act in (e.g. w/projects/) or a DID URL (e.g. did:key:z6Mk…/w/)

can.description: Ability (e.g. job/read, job/manage, job/message for Jobs; crud/read or crud/write for raw data; * for all)

exp.description: Optional expiry as a future integer Unix timestamp in seconds. Omit or set to null for a genuinely non-expiring token; the emitted token carries an explicit exp:null claim.

prf.description: Optional proofs: UCAN JWTs granting this venue the capabilities it passes on. Only the venue itself may supply them. Omitted or empty mints a root.

key.description: Optional held key to sign with instead of the venue's key: its did:key, multibase public key or 0x account key in your keyring, or <did>/x/crypto/keys/<key> in another holder's. The grant's issuer is that key's did:key, bare paths are under it, and it may name only resources that did:key is root of: its own and those of identities nested below it. Needs key/sign/grant on it.

output.description: Complete signed UCAN token (header, payload, sig)

iss.description: Its issuer: the venue's DID, or the did:key of the held key that signed it.
